Warhammer Age of Sigmar

Age of Sigmar replaced Warhammer Fantasy Battle in 2015, shifting from ranked infantry blocks to hero-focused skirmish and mass battle in a high-fantasy setting. The miniature scale matches modern Warhammer 40k — all new GW fantasy releases since 2015 are 32mm heroic.

Scale Details

Miniature Scale
32mm
Ratio Equivalent
1:50
Measurement
eye level
Eye Level Height
32.0mm

AoS uses the same 32mm heroic scale as Warhammer 40k Primaris. Older Warhammer Fantasy miniatures (pre-2015) were 28mm heroic and remain usable in Age of Sigmar and The Old World, though they sit slightly shorter than modern sculpts.

Publisher: Games Workshop · Base Sizes: 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm, 60mm, 80mm, 100mm, 120mm

3D Printing Tips for AoS

AoS models tend to have dramatic poses with flowing cloaks and extended weapons. Print character models with 0.2mm nozzle for crisp edges on armor and chainmail. Large centerpiece models (Morrknul, Nagash) benefit from 0.04-0.06mm layers on resin. FDM works well for terrain and monsters at 0.1mm layers.

Frequently Asked Questions

What scale is Warhammer Age of Sigmar?
Warhammer Age of Sigmar miniatures are 32mm scale (1:50 ratio), measured eye level. AoS uses the same 32mm heroic scale as Warhammer 40k Primaris. Older Warhammer Fantasy miniatures (pre-2015) were 28mm heroic and remain usable in Age of Sigmar and The Old World, though they sit slightly shorter than modern sculpts.
What base sizes does Warhammer Age of Sigmar use?
Warhammer Age of Sigmar uses the following base sizes: 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm, 60mm, 80mm, 100mm, 120mm.
What nozzle and layer height should I use for Warhammer Age of Sigmar miniatures?
AoS models tend to have dramatic poses with flowing cloaks and extended weapons. Print character models with 0.2mm nozzle for crisp edges on armor and chainmail. Large centerpiece models (Morrknul, Nagash) benefit from 0.04-0.06mm layers on resin. FDM works well for terrain and monsters at 0.1mm layers.
